directAnswer: Pope Honorius III was Cencio, a Roman cleric and longtime papal treasurer, who reigned from 1216 to 1227. He approved the Dominican Order, the final Rule of St. Francis and the Carmelite rule, launched the Fifth Crusade, and crowned Frederick II emperor.

sections.h2: Cencio, Camerarius and Author of the Liber Censuum
paras: Cencio was born in Rome; his traditional identification with the Savelli family is doubted by many historians. He was a canon of Santa Maria Maggiore and served as camerarius, the official in charge of papal finances. In 1192 he compiled the Liber Censuum, a register of the revenues owed to the Roman Church that remains a key source for medieval history.

Celestine III made him a cardinal, and he is often said to have been a tutor to the young Frederick II. He was elected at Perugia on July 18, 1216, two days after the death of Innocent III, when he was already elderly.

Honorius gave formal approval to several religious families that shaped the Church for centuries. On December 22, 1216, he confirmed the Order of Preachers founded by St. Dominic. On November 29, 1223, his bull Solet annuere approved the definitive Rule of the Friars Minor written by St. Francis, the text Franciscans still follow.

In 1226 he approved the rule given to the hermits of Mount Carmel by St. Albert of Jerusalem, a step in the recognition of the Carmelites. He also supported the Third Order movements that offered lay men and women a structured penitential life.

sections.h2: The Fifth Crusade and Frederick II
paras: Honorius made the recovery of Jerusalem the central goal of his reign. The Fifth Crusade sailed from 1217 and captured the Egyptian port of Damietta in 1219, but the crusaders refused an offer to exchange it for Jerusalem, marched on Cairo, and were forced to surrender in 1221.

Frederick II had taken the cross in 1215, and Honorius crowned him emperor in Rome on November 22, 1220, in expectation that he would lead the crusade. Frederick repeatedly delayed, and in 1225 at San Germano he agreed to set out by 1227 under pain of excommunication. Honorius did not live to see the outcome.

Honorius issued the Compilatio quinta, a collection of decretals sent to the University of Bologna in 1226, one of the first official papal law books. He was known for patience and mildness, preferring negotiation to confrontation. He died in Rome on March 18, 1227, and was buried in Santa Maria Maggiore.

keyFacts: Personal name: Cencio, of Rome; papal camerarius
Approved the Dominicans (1216), the Franciscan Rule (1223) and the Carmelite rule (1226)
Crowned Frederick II emperor on November 22, 1220

faqs.question: Which religious orders did Honorius III approve?
faqs.answer: He confirmed the Dominicans in 1216, approved the final Rule of St. Francis with the bull Solet annuere in 1223, and approved the Carmelite rule in 1226.

faqs.question: What was the Liber Censuum?
faqs.answer: A register of payments owed to the Roman Church, compiled by Cencio in 1192 while he was papal treasurer. Historians still rely on it.

faqs.question: How did the Fifth Crusade turn out?
faqs.answer: Crusaders captured Damietta in Egypt in 1219, but after a failed advance on Cairo they surrendered the city in 1221 without regaining Jerusalem.
